headline: 6 token contracts catalogued across Ethereum, BSC, Solana, Sui, Plume Mainnet, and Stellar; proxy admin and owner addresses not yet resolved due to on-chain fetch limits.

findings.text: D1: Etherscan search confirmed XAUM ERC-20 token at 0x2103E845C5E135493Bb6c2A4f0B8651956eA8682 on Ethereum (proxy contract per Etherscan label). BscScan search confirmed XAUM BEP-20 token at 0x23AE4fd8E7844cdBc97775496eBd0E8248656028 on BSC. Plume Mainnet explorer link surfaced from official website (not independently fetched). No Etherscan name-tag search endpoint was directly reachable; addresses confirmed via CoinGecko and official product page cross-references.

D2: Official XAUm product page at matrixdock.com/xaum lists all deployed token addresses per chain inline. Gitbook docs at matrixdock.gitbook.io has a 'Contract Address' sub-page under Smart Contract section; fetch was not completed due to tool call limit. No single canonical 'Deployed contracts' doc page URL was fully verified, though the gitbook path is identified.

D3: Gitbook docs reference a 'Contract Audit' section and physical vault audit reports by Bureau Veritas. The audit link URL pattern is matrixdock.gitbook.io/matrixdock-docs/english/gold-token-xaum/smart-contract/contract-audit but was not fetched this run. No audit_links were pinned in the per-protocol context. Audit firm names and report URLs remain unknown.

D4: No GitHub repo is recorded in protocol.github (listed as 'none recorded'). A search for GitHub artifacts was not productive. No deployment artifacts (Foundry broadcast, hardhat-deploy, addresses.json) could be located from any GitHub source.

D5: Chains in scope: Binance (BSC), Ethereum, Sui, Solana, Plume Mainnet. Token address found per chain from official product page: Ethereum 0x2103E845C5E135493Bb6c2A4f0B8651956eA8682, BSC 0x23AE4fd8E7844cdBc97775496eBd0E8248656028, Solana 5aLhp9VnUEKcsdtkfsf2DUgpJfomx7GmYVny24dHUZoB, Sui package 0x9d297676e7a4b771ab023291377b2adfaa4938fb9080b8d12430e4b108b836a9, Plume 0xA0C4F78A29ead4ABf6b7f5B3F0d05C0f3EAb8DDf. Stellar also listed (not in protocol.chains). No zero-result chains; all five chains have at least one token address confirmed from official product page.

D6: No factory contracts identified in available sources. XAUm is a single-token deployment per chain, not a factory pattern. The PoR Oracle on Ethereum mainnet is referenced in docs but its address was not surfaced from fetched sources.
D7: Token role assigned to all six chain deployments. Admin/owner/proxy_admin role assignments cannot be made without on-chain reads; no admin addresses were surfaced from fetched sources this run.
D8: All addresses in admin_addresses[] trace to the official product page fetch (matrixdock.com/xaum). No snippet-only sightings were promoted to admin_addresses[].

rationale.verdict: Discovery walk covered official website, XAUm product page, Gitbook docs index, PoR docs page, BscScan and Etherscan search results, and CoinGecko. Six token contract addresses were catalogued across six chains from the official product page. Proxy admin, owner, and PoR Oracle addresses remain unresolved due to on-chain read fetch limits and the absence of a pinned GitHub repo or audits. Grade is unknown pending proxy/admin enumeration.

protocol_metadata.about: MatrixDock XAUM (XAUm) is a tokenized gold product where each token represents one troy ounce of LBMA-accredited physical gold (99.99% purity) stored in custodian vaults in Singapore and Hong Kong. Users can mint XAUm by subscribing with USDC/USDT and redeem for cash or physical gold delivery; a 0.25% fee applies to both mint and redemption. XAUm is deployed natively across Ethereum, BNB Chain, Solana, Sui, Plume Mainnet, and Stellar, with cross-chain mint budgets enforced by a Proof-of-Reserve (PoR) Oracle on Ethereum that caps total supply across all chains to match verified physical reserves. The token adheres to both ERC-20/BEP-20 (fungible) and ERC-721/BEP-721 (NFT, for fixed bar allocation) standards, and is integrated into DeFi lending and DEX protocols including Morpho, CurveLend, Venus, and PancakeSwap.
